title: November 2026 Hindu Festival Calendar: Diwali on November 8, Chhath and Dev Diwali Dates
excerpt: Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, Chhath arghya on Sunday, November 15 and Dev Diwali on Tuesday, November 24 — the full November 2026 calendar with weekend flags for diaspora families.
body:
• Diwali (Lakshmi Puja) falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, opening with Dhanteras on Friday, November 6 and closing with Bhai Dooj on Wednesday, November 11.
  • Chhath Puja runs November 13-16: Nahay-Khay on November 13, Kharna on November 14, evening arghya on Sunday, November 15 and morning arghya on November 16.
  • Dev Diwali, Kartik Purnima and Guru Nanak Jayanti all fall on Tuesday, November 24, while Dev Uthani Ekadashi is on Friday, November 20 and Tulsi Vivah on Saturday, November 21.
  • For diaspora families, Diwali and the main Chhath arghya both fall on Sundays in 2026, so no weekday leave is needed for the two biggest observances — check your local temple panchang, as tithi timings vary by city.

November 2026 is dominated by a single, late festival season. Because of Adhik Maas earlier in the year, Diwali arrives in November rather than October, and the month packs the five days of Diwali, the four days of Chhath, Dev Uthani Ekadashi and Dev Diwali into just over three weeks, according to festival calendars published by TyoharKosh and Boldsky.

The Five Days of Diwali, November 6-11

The season opens on Sunday, November 1 with Ahoi Ashtami, the fast mothers keep for their children, followed by Rama Ekadashi on Thursday, November 5. Dhanteras on Friday, November 6 is the first day of Diwali, honouring Lord Dhanvantari and marked by buying metal, a utensil or a small piece of gold or silver, and lighting the Yama Deepam at the doorstep in the evening. In New Delhi, the Dhanteras puja muhurat listed by TyoharKosh is 6:02 p.m. to 7:57 p.m.

Saturday, November 7 is Kali Chaudas and Naraka Chaturdashi, known as Choti Diwali, when the first rows of lamps are lit. The pre-dawn abhyang snan falls on the morning of Sunday, November 8 because Chaturdashi is the tithi at sunrise that day, and that evening is Diwali itself — Lakshmi Puja on Kartik Amavasya, with a New Delhi muhurat of 5:54 p.m. to 7:50 p.m. in the calendars consulted. Monday, November 9 is a gap day in several panchangs this year, with Govardhan Puja and Annakut on Tuesday, November 10 and Bhai Dooj on Wednesday, November 11, when sisters perform the tilak ceremony for their brothers. Some regional calendars list Govardhan Puja a day earlier, so families should confirm with their local panchang.

Chhath Puja, November 13-16

Chhath, centred in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh and now widely observed by diaspora communities at rivers, lakes and community pools, runs over four days. Nahay-Khay, with a ritual bath and a simple meal, is on Friday, November 13. Kharna, a day-long fast broken after sunset with kheer and roti, is on Saturday, November 14. The main evening offering, Sandhya Arghya to the setting sun, is on Sunday, November 15, and the fast concludes with Usha Arghya to the rising sun on Monday, November 16. The fast is often kept without water for about 36 hours.

Dev Uthani, Tulsi Vivah and Dev Diwali

Dev Uthani Ekadashi, also called Prabodhini Ekadashi, falls on Friday, November 20. It marks the awakening of Lord Vishnu after the four months of Chaturmas, and the fast is broken after sunrise on November 21. Tulsi Vivah, the ceremonial wedding of the tulsi plant to Vishnu, follows on Saturday, November 21.

The month closes on Tuesday, November 24 with a triple observance: Kartik Purnima, Dev Diwali — also called Dev Deepawali or Tripurari Purnima, when Varanasi lines its ghats with lamps — and Guru Nanak Jayanti, marked with kirtan and langar at gurdwaras. Guru Tegh Bahadur's Martyrdom Day is also listed on the same date in the calendars consulted.

What This Means for Diaspora Families

The 2026 calendar is unusually kind on weekends. Diwali on Sunday, November 8 and the Chhath evening arghya on Sunday, November 15 mean families in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom can observe the two biggest festivals without taking a weekday off, while Dhanteras on a Friday evening and Tulsi Vivah on a Saturday also fall outside working hours for most people. Govardhan Puja on Tuesday, November 10, Bhai Dooj on Wednesday, November 11 and Dev Diwali on Tuesday, November 24 are weekday observances, so temple visits those days will be evening events for working families.

Timings, not just dates, matter. Lakshmi Puja is done in Pradosh Kaal after sunset, Chhath arghya is tied to local sunset and sunrise, and Ekadashi parana depends on the tithi in your city. The calendars cited here calculate tithis for New Delhi, and both sources warn that regional panchangs can keep a festival a day apart. Check your local temple's calendar before finalising puja, travel or leave plans.
